title: The Face of Another is Essential Cinema

commenti.body:
Honestly I've only read Kobo Abes novel so many years ago now.  Haven't seen the movie!  

I think this sort of thing is almost a trope of its age.  But a good one. 
Plastic surgery was on the rise.  
Jungian psychology was on the rise.  

It was the age of psychology and persona.  Watch Ingmar Bergman's 'Persona.' 

There was a trend with the idea of masks, identity, etc. 

The BBC  documentary by Adam Curtis 'Century of The Self' focuses on this.  Much of his work too.  

I did see 'Face of Another.'  I see all of these things as direct decendents of what was becoming popular at that time: psychoanalysis, self exploration, ideas of personality, etc.  

They're all still very prevalent today.  But at that time they were quite new and experiencing widespread interest.

Great write up. It's a shame Teshigahara has been relatively forgotten compared to other great Japanese directors. In my opinion, he belongs right there in the conversation with the best. Perhaps it's the relatively artsy style of his films that make them a bit harder for audiences to latch onto the way they do someone like Kurosawa.
